chapter: Paris, Lester Young, drugs, Mississippi and later sessions
title: The Woodside group: checkers with Clyde Hart and Prez after the war
summary: In New York the Woodside group rehearsed daily with Betty Roche singing and Clyde Hart brought in; after the war Collins saw Prez was burned out.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: So they would always try to get me to come to New York, you know, to -- so finally when I did go there we just got together right away. You know, as a matter of fact he had just left Basie, and we just took up where we left off in Chicago. And we played every day. We would go downstairs in the hotel, in the Woodside Hotel, and play every day, as I told you, without piano. We would just have piano -- I mean guitar, bass, drums, Prez, and Shad Collins, and finally Betty Roche started dropping in and so she became our vocalist. She would sing with us every day. She was there every day. And finally I mean, eventually I brought Clyde in.

Clyde Hart. I asked Clyde, because I used to play checkers with Clyde every night. Me, John Williams who was Mary Lou Williams' husband, and Joe Jones who thought he could play checkers. And this was every night. So I prevailed upon Clyde to come by rehearsal, and he played and eventually he just started working with us. You know, but Lester, yes. This is why I told you when I saw him after the war, I detected right away that something had happened to him. I could see it right away, because I knew him so well.
He wasn't the same, you know. Something had -- he
looked like he was burned out. You know, he was playing -- you had to know him well to tell this, but I knew this. That something had happened.
